content: Albuterol is a medication prescribed to prevent and treat wheezing, difficulty breathing, and chest tightness caused by lung diseases such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It is also used to prevent breathing difficulties during exercise. Albuterol belongs to a class of medications called bronchodilators, which work by relaxing and opening the air passages to the lungs, making breathing easier. Albuterol is available as a liquid solution for inhalation using a nebulizer and as an aerosol for inhalation using an inhaler. When used to treat or prevent symptoms of lung disease, the aerosol is typically used every 4 to 6 hours as needed. For exercise-induced breathing difficulties, it is usually used 15 to 30 minutes before exercise. The nebulizer solution is generally used three or four times a day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use albuterol exactly as directed and do not use more or less of it or more frequently than prescribed. Contact your doctor if your symptoms worsen or if you feel that albuterol is no longer effective in controlling your symptoms. If you find yourself needing to use albuterol more often than usual, inform your doctor. Albuterol helps control symptoms of asthma and other lung diseases but does not cure them. Do not stop using albuterol without consulting your doctor. If you are using the inhaler, the medication comes in canisters, each designed to provide 200 inhalations. After the labeled number of inhalations has been used, the canister may not deliver the correct amount of medication, even if it still contains liquid and releases a spray when pressed. Discard the canister after the labeled number of inhalations. Some inhalers come with an attached counter to track the number of sprays used. Do not attempt to alter the counter or remove it from the canister. When the counter shows 020, contact your doctor or pharmacist to refill your prescription. When the counter shows 000, stop using that canister and discard it. If your inhaler does not have a counter, keep track of the number of inhalations used. Divide the total number of inhalations in the canister by the number of inhalations you use daily to estimate how long the inhaler will last. Do not float the canister in water to check if it contains medication. Use the inhaler only with its designated albuterol canister and do not use it to inhale other medications. Avoid getting albuterol in your eyes. Do not use the inhaler near flames or heat sources, as it may explode if exposed to high temperatures. Before using albuterol for the first time, read the written instructions provided with the inhaler or nebulizer. Ask your doctor, pharmacist, or respiratory therapist to demonstrate its use and practice using it under their supervision. If your child will be using the inhaler, ensure they know how to use it correctly and supervise them each time they use it. To use the aerosol inhaler, follow these steps: 1. Remove the protective dust cap from the mouthpiece and ensure the canister is fully and firmly inserted. 2. If using the inhaler for the first time, or if it has not been used in over 14 days, prime it by shaking it well and pressing down on the canister four times to release four sprays into the air, away from your face. Avoid getting albuterol in your eyes. 3. Shake the inhaler well. 4. Exhale completely through your mouth. 5. Hold the canister with the mouthpiece at the bottom, facing you, and the canister pointing upward. Place the open end of the mouthpiece into your mouth and close your lips tightly around it. 6. Press down once on the container to spray the medication into your mouth while inhaling deeply and slowly. 7. Hold your breath for 10 seconds, then remove the inhaler and exhale slowly. 8. If instructed to use two puffs, wait one minute and repeat steps 3–7. 9. Replace the protective cap on the inhaler. To use the nebulizer solution, follow these steps: 1. Remove one vial of albuterol solution from the foil pouch, leaving the remaining vials in the pouch until ready for use. 2. Inspect the liquid in the vial. It should be clear and colorless. Do not use the vial if the liquid is cloudy or discolored. 3. Twist off the top of the vial and squeeze all the liquid into the nebulizer reservoir. If using other medications with the nebulizer, consult your doctor or pharmacist about combining them with albuterol in the reservoir. 4. Connect the nebulizer reservoir to the mouthpiece or face mask. 5. Attach the nebulizer to the compressor. 6. Place the mouthpiece in your mouth or put on the face mask. Sit upright in a comfortable position and turn on the compressor. 7. Breathe in calmly, deeply, and evenly for about 5–15 minutes until the mist stops forming in the nebulizer chamber. Clean your inhaler or nebulizer regularly. Failure to clean the inhaler properly may result in blockages, preventing it from spraying medication. If this occurs, follow the manufacturer’s cleaning instructions to remove the blockage. Inhaled albuterol is sometimes used to treat or improve muscle paralysis in patients with conditions causing paralysis attacks. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. Albuterol may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before using albuterol, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to albuterol, levalbuterol, or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and non-prescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Mention any beta blockers, digoxin, diuretics, epinephrine, other inhaled medications, antidepressants, or monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) you are using or have recently stopped using. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had an irregular heartbeat, heart disease, high blood pressure, hyperthyroidism, diabetes, or seizures. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while using albuterol, contact your doctor immediately. Albuterol inhalation may sometimes cause wheezing and difficulty breathing immediately after use. If this occurs, call your doctor right away and do not use albuterol again unless instructed to do so. If you miss a dose of albuterol and are on a regular schedule, use the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not use a double dose to make up for a missed one. Albuterol may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience uncontrollable shaking, nervousness, headache, nausea, vomiting, cough, throat irritation, or muscle, bone, or back pain. Serious side effects include fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeat, chest pain, rash, hives, itching, swelling, increased difficulty breathing, difficulty swallowing, or hoarseness. If you experience any of these, contact your doctor immediately. Report any unusual problems while using this medication to your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store albuterol in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture. Discard outdated or no longer needed medication. If using the nebulizer solution, discard vials one week after removing them from the foil pouch. If using an inhaler with an attached counter, discard it two months after removing it from the foil pouch. Consult your pharmacist about proper disposal. Do not puncture the aerosol canister or discard it in an incinerator or fire. In case of overdose, call your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the victim has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include seizures, chest pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, nervousness, headache, uncontrollable shaking, dry mouth, nausea, dizziness, excessive tiredness, lack of energy, or difficulty sleeping. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
